sections.content: [Placeholder passage text for The coconut palm. The passage covers the many uses of the coconut palm: the trunk provides timber for houses and furniture; leaves (up to 6 metres) for brushes; flower stems provide sap for drink or sugar; the fruit layers provide coir fibres for rope/matting, shell as fuel and for containers, coconut water as a drink and fertiliser for plants, and coconut flesh for oil/milk for cooking and cosmetics, and glycerine used in soap. The passage also discusses how coconuts spread around the world, their germination, and their spread to/from America and Asia.]
